newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Activists from Hong Kong and Taiwan trying to sail to the disputed Diaoyu islands were confronted and stopped by a flotilla of Japanese coast guard vessels.

-- The Chinese navy held large-scale exercises in the East China Sea recently. Sources said the wargames were related to the dispute over the Diaoyu islands and territorial arguments with the Philippines.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese military leader Zhang Zhen stressed that the People's Liberation Army's entry into Hong Kong on July 1 would be an important symbol of Chinese rule.
-- The Chinese government expressed its determination to safeguard the sovereignty of the Diaoyu islands and warned Japan to realise the seriousness of the problem and stop making trouble.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) figures showed the number of mortgage loans reached a record high in April. The head of the HKMA warned banks to show restraint in mortgage lending.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Legislative Council is seeking to mothball a controversial pension plan -- the Mandatory Provident Fund -- until after the handover, saying it is too complex and extensive to review accurately before June 30.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Analysts said Cathay Pacific Airways could lose up to two percent of its net profit, or HK$200 million, due to the grounding of its Airbus A330 aircraft over engine problems.
